analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The checkout is shallow with depth 50, so historical conclusions are limited to the three available commits. The repository is small: all 33 tracked files were inventoried, and all substantive source, documentation, and tests were inspected. The generated HTML fixtures and uv.lock were not reviewed line by line.

stated_purpose: Provide a Codex-driven autonomous experiment loop that improves one web scraper by editing scraper.py, executing and scoring each hypothesis, and retaining only score-improving commits.

observed_capabilities.statement: The CLI can initialize isolated Git worktree sessions, bootstrap an HTML cache, run bounded cached or live optimization iterations, and report session status.

Each iteration prompts Codex with the target contract and recent results, rejects changes outside scraper.py, compiles and executes the scraper, scores its output, and keeps or resets the resulting commit.
The evaluator scores record yield, required and optional field coverage, type castability, uniqueness, and observed HTTP block rate using fixed weights.

The included Books to Scrape baseline extracts 40 fixture-backed records with required title, price, currency, and availability fields, while deliberately withholding already-computed rating and URL candidates from its output.

SmartClient combines deterministic disk caching, adaptive per-domain delays, proxy selection, browser-header rotation, response block classification, retries, statistics, and optional Playwright fetching.
Agent responses are analyzed for structured RALPH_STATUS fields and completion signals, which feed a dual-condition loop exit gate and subsequent prompt feedback.

planned_work.statement: The implementation-status document lists circuit-breaker integration, resumable session continuity, API-call limiting, monitoring, and broader integration and end-to-end testing as pending work.

architecture.statement: Human-controlled strategy and target configuration are separated from the agent-editable scraper and from frozen orchestration, evaluation, schema, and HTTP infrastructure.

loop.py is the orchestration entry point; it creates per-session worktrees and generated run artifacts, invokes Codex, delegates fetching and parsing to scraper.py, and calls evaluate.py before committing or rolling back experiments.

The architecture is intentionally reusable for other scraping targets through targets.py, program.md, and a new baseline scraper, although only the Books to Scrape campaign is implemented and fixture-tested here.

accomplishments.statement: The repository contains an end-to-end autonomous experimentation harness rather than only a specification or generated scaffold.

Thirty test functions cover evaluator behavior, cached fixture parsing, HTTP defense components, browser-mode boundaries, loop keep/discard/crash flows, forbidden edits, timeouts, response analysis, and the standalone circuit breaker.
The analysis notebook provides code for summarizing experiment outcomes, improvements, and progress plots from a generated results.tsv file.

gaps.statement: No committed experiment history, scrape result, run log, or progress visualization demonstrates that the autonomous workflow has completed a real campaign.
The circuit-breaker implementation is imported only by its standalone test script and is not constructed or consulted by loop.py.
There is no CI, release, deployment, scheduling, or monitoring configuration to establish repeatable operational use.
The baseline intentionally omits all optional output fields even though it already computes candidate values for them, leaving the checked-in scraper below the evaluator's attainable score.
Documentation calls the Ralph-enhanced system production-grade while simultaneously recording missing circuit-breaker integration, continuity, monitoring, and enhanced testing.

risks.statement: Codex runs in full-auto mode before changed paths are checked; the post-execution Git diff guard proves file-scope cleanup but does not prove that command, network, or other side effects were constrained during execution.
The autonomous loop lacks the stronger circuit-breaker safeguard described in the status document because that component is not integrated into the runtime path.
README setup requires OPENAI_API_KEY, but .gitignore has no .env pattern; this increases accidental credential-commit risk even though no credential file is currently tracked.
Live-mode scores depend on an external website and block-detection heuristics, so fixture-backed success alone would not establish reliable behavior against changing or protected targets.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Confirm whether the latest commit's explicit archive intent is final; if so, archive the repository with a short note that it is a scraper-autoresearch prototype and leave the current implementation unchanged.
If development resumes, integrate the existing circuit breaker into run_loop and add tests proving that repeated no-progress, repeated-error, and permission-denial conditions halt agent execution.
Run and preserve one reproducible cached campaign plus a controlled live validation, recording dependency versions, scores, and artifacts so the primary workflow has execution evidence.
Add .env and common credential-file patterns to .gitignore before any further local API-key setup.

questions: Was the July 11 commit intended to precede permanent GitHub archival, and has that archival action been completed?
Was an autonomous cached or live campaign ever run successfully outside the repository, and are its results worth preserving?
Should the unintegrated circuit breaker and Ralph status work remain as reference code or be completed?
Is the framework expected to support targets beyond Books to Scrape, or was it a one-off autoresearch experiment?

evidence.summary: Owner-supplied snapshot identifies a private main-branch repository pushed on 2026-07-11 with no description, open issues, or open pull requests.
Describes the autonomous edit-run-score-keep/discard loop, prerequisites, CLI, evaluation model, exit conditions, operating modes, and adaptation workflow.
Restricts the inner agent to scraper.py, prioritizes optional Books to Scrape fields, and defines the RALPH_STATUS response convention.

Marks response analysis, dual-condition exit logic, and a standalone circuit breaker complete while listing breaker integration, session continuity, rate limiting, monitoring, and enhanced testing as pending.
Defines Python 3.12+, scraping and analysis dependencies, optional Playwright browser support, pytest development support, and a Hatch-built autoscrape package.
Configures two Books to Scrape pages, a 40-record seven-field schema, runtime and delay bounds, caching, and disabled-by-default browser automation.

Implements session worktrees, Codex invocation, post-run edit-scope validation, compilation, execution, scoring, commit retention or reset, live validation, result logging, and bounded exit conditions.
Constrains the inner agent's final result to a description, hypothesis, risk level, and expected score effect.
Implements the Books to Scrape baseline using SmartClient and BeautifulSoup; required fields are emitted while computed rating, image URL, and detail URL candidates are removed before output.
Implements the six-component weighted score and resilient loading of scrape JSON and SmartClient statistics.
Provides HTTP caching, requests or Playwright fetching, adaptive delays, proxy health management, browser-header rotation, retries, block classification, and request statistics.
Parses RALPH_STATUS blocks and classifies completion indicators, exit signals, work type, no-work patterns, test-only behavior, and errors.
Implements a persistent CLOSED, OPEN, and HALF_OPEN breaker for no progress, repeated errors, output decline, and permission failures, but is not referenced by loop.py.
Contains evaluator, infrastructure, browser-mode, and autonomous-loop tests, including mocked keep, discard, crash, forbidden-edit, and timeout flows.
Two saved listing pages support assertions that the parser finds 40 records with normalized required fields and recognizes star ratings.
Exercises response analysis and the standalone persistent circuit breaker, including cooldown recovery.
Contains Python 3.12 cells for loading results.tsv, summarizing outcomes, ranking kept improvements, and plotting experiment progress.
Only .gitkeep placeholders are present; experiment history and generated run artifacts are ignored and absent from the checkout.
Ignores generated results, worktrees, proxy configuration, caches, and output, but does not ignore .env files; no credential-named file is tracked.
The 33-file tracked tree contains Python source, tests, two HTML fixtures, documentation, a notebook, and dependency metadata, with no CI, deployment, or release configuration.

The shallow clone exposes three commits: the March 12 scaffold and cache fix, followed by 1f2a7ae on 2026-07-11 titled 'Save latest changes before archiving'; only main/origin-main and no tags are present.

confidence.rationale: Primary source, documentation, fixtures, and extensive test code agree that this is a substantive autonomous-scraping prototype, and the unintegrated breaker and absent artifacts are directly observable. Confidence is limited because read-only constraints prevented executing the write-heavy tests or workflow, no CI or run artifacts provide independent verification, live private GitHub state was unavailable, and history is shallow.

limitations: Tests and the end-to-end workflow were not executed because they create temporary repositories, caches, commits, and output files, which conflicts with the read-only analysis constraint.
No generated experiment evidence was available to establish achieved scores, real Codex behavior, live-site reliability, or actual usage.
The shallow clone contains only three commits, so earlier or removed development history cannot be assessed.
The supplied metadata does not state whether GitHub's archived flag is currently enabled.
No secret values were read; credential analysis was limited to filenames, tracked-file inventory, documentation requirements, and ignore rules.
